newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Huge volumes force shutdown on German bourse.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Huge volumes force shutdown on German bourse.

text.p: Massive volumes amid soaring prices on German financial markets overloaded trading systems and forced a temporary stock market shutdown on Wednesday, the German bourse said.

While a stronger dollar pushed the DAX leading share index to flirt with levels unseen before and debt prices set new contract highs as U.S. interest rate expectations were scaled back, all floor trade in equities, bonds and derivatives was temporarily suspended.

"We expect to have completed 3.5 million transactions by the end of the day," Werner Seifert, chief executive of the German bourse said in a statement. "That is almost twice as many as on the heavy volume days after the launch of Deutsche Telekom shares."
But Seifert said the bourse would act quickly to increase the capacity of trading systems.
"By Saturday at the latest, capacities will be 3.5 million plus 'X' percent," Seifert told Reuters, adding :"X" certainly means more than five percent."

Even after the initial offering of shares in Deutsche Telekom in November last year -- Germany's biggest stock market flotation -- volume peaked at only around 1.9 million transactions, the bourse said.

On Wednesday, floor trade was halted for a full hour starting at 1015 GMT, the statement said, while trade on the IBIS electronic system was interrupted from 0850 GMT to 0915 GMT, and again from 1005 GMT until 1310 GMT.
As a result of the interruptions, floor trading hours were extended to close at 1230 GMT instead of the usual 1130 close.
A spokesman from the bourse told Reuters that dealing on the DTB futures exchange was undisturbed.

The stocks disruption followed a trading break on Monday when IBIS computer trade was stopped for 90 minutes and the opening of bourse floor trade delayed for about two hours due to computer network problems.
Seifert said the shutdowns had not cost market players in volume terms, because trading times had been extended. "Also no investor has been badly affected," Seifert said.
German stock and bond markets were racing higher as business was halted, with the DAX index having reached a new record high of 4,418.64 points in early trade.
A key speech on the U.S. economy, delivered by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan late on Tuesday, was behind the gains, traders said.
While Greenspan said that interest rates might have to rise in the U.S. to curb price pressure, he suggested a monetary tightening was not imminent, boosting Wall Street and the dollar.

The DAX share index closed 4.15 percent higher on the day at 4,406.09, up 175.67 points. In the debt markets, the 10-year benchmark Bund was at 103.64 for a bid yield of 5.507 percent, while the DTB September Bund future was 23 basis points higher at 103.24 by 1412 GMT.
